newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end down in quiet trade, Autoliv up.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end down in quiet trade, Autoliv up.

text.p: Swedish shares ended lower on Monday in quiet, trendless trade with car safety equipment company Autoliv in focus.
The general index fell 0.21 percent to 3,172.55 in below average turnover of 2.47 billion crowns.
Autoliv presented a six-month profit of $177 million, which was somewhat higher than the $169 million analysts expected.
The share came off day-highs of 302 crowns on the news and ended at 295.5 crowns, up 2.5 crowns from its Friday close.
"Speculation drove the share higher ahead of the report," a trader said.
"But the report was slightly better than expected, or roughly in line with expectations," he added.
Bank shares were mixed with Swedbank rising five crowns to 180 while Handelsbanken dropped 4.5 to 255.5 crowns.
"Interest rates have fallen some lately and Handelsbanken rose a while ago. I think Swedbank was just catching up. Many probably changed from Handelsbanken to Swedbank," a trader said.
Telecoms group Ericsson fell five crowns to 359 on profit taking after rising last week when it presented its six-month earnings.
